# glinet_multiwan (Resource)

Manages the multi-WAN mode of the router (`kmwan.set_config` in the router API): failover or load balance between the WAN interfaces, for example `wan`, `secondwan`, `wwan` (repeater) and `tethering`. The router has one multi-WAN configuration, so use one instance of this resource.

~> **Warning:** a write can change the uplink that the router uses, and so can cut the Internet access of the router and of its clients.

In failover mode, the router uses the online interface that comes first in `priority`. In load balance mode, it divides the traffic between the online interfaces by their `weights`. The tracking of each interface is in `glinet_multiwan_interface`, the sensitivity of the tracking is in `glinet_multiwan_sensitivity`, and the state of the interfaces is in the data source `glinet_multiwan_status`. The provider writes only when the router values differ from the configuration, so a create whose values are equal to those of the router sends no write. A failover write does not send the weights, and a load balance write does not send the metrics, as the web UI does. It is not known whether the router keeps them. So the provider reads `priority` only in failover mode and `weights` only in load balance mode; the attribute of the other mode is null. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Failover: the router uses the wired WAN, and the repeater when the wired WAN is offline.
# The interfaces that are not in the list come after the listed ones.
resource "glinet_multiwan" "this" {
  mode     = "failover"
  priority = ["wan", "wwan"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mode` (String) Multi-WAN mode: `failover` or `load_balance` (`mode` `0` or `1` in the router API).

### Optional

- `priority` (List of String) Names of the interfaces in the failover order, the first one first. Can be set only when `mode` is `failover`. The provider sends the metrics 1, 2, 3 and so on in this order (`metric` in the router API). As the web UI does, it sends all interfaces of the router: the interfaces that are not in the list come after the listed ones, in their current order on the router. So the list can have only the first interfaces of the order; the provider then compares the list with the first interfaces of the router order. Create and update fail without a write when an interface is not on the router. When it is not set, the order on the router does not change: the provider sends the current order.
- `weights` (Map of Number) Weight from 0 to 10 of each interface, by interface name (`weight` in the router API). Can be set only when `mode` is `load_balance`. The provider sends the weights of all interfaces of the router: an interface that is not in the map keeps its current weight. The web UI does not send the interfaces that it does not show (`hidden_features` of `system.get_info`); the provider sends them with their current weight. The provider compares only the interfaces of the map with the router. Create and update fail without a write when an interface is not on the router. The web UI warns when fewer than two interfaces have a weight that is not 0. What weight 0 does is not known. When it is not set, the weights on the router do not change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `multiwan`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "multiwan".
terraform import glinet_multiwan.this multiwan
```
